signals.name: US equity stress
signals.why: The S&P 500 is the world's risk barometer; sharp falls and spiking volatility transmit to pensions, credit and confidence globally.
signals.drivers: Earnings, interest-rate expectations, liquidity, geopolitical shocks, positioning and leverage.

rubric.alert: VIX > 30, or drawdown > 15%, or a market-wide circuit breaker trips.
rubric.watch: VIX 20–30, or drawdown 5–15%.
rubric.normal: VIX < 20 and S&P 500 drawdown from 52-week high < 5%.

signals.name: FTSE 100
signals.why: The UK's main index — a gauge of UK-listed multinationals, pensions and sterling-area sentiment.
signals.drivers: Commodity prices, sterling, global risk appetite, UK policy and banking sector news.

rubric.alert: Drawdown > 12%, or a single-day fall > 4%.
rubric.watch: Drawdown 5–12%, or a single-day fall > 2.5% this week.
rubric.normal: Drawdown from 52-week high < 5% and no single-day fall > 2.5% this week.

signals.name: Bond market volatility
signals.why: US Treasuries price almost every asset on earth; when the 'risk-free' market becomes volatile, funding and collateral chains strain.
signals.drivers: Inflation data, Fed path, deficits and auction demand, foreign holder flows, liquidity.

rubric.alert: MOVE > 140, or disorderly Treasury trading (failed/tailed auctions with Fed action, emergency buybacks).
rubric.watch: MOVE 100–140, or US 10y moved ≥ 40bp in a month, or weak auctions flagged.
rubric.normal: MOVE index < 100 and US 10y moved < 40bp over the past month.

signals.name: Credit spreads
signals.why: High-yield spreads show how much lenders demand to fund weaker companies — an early warning of defaults and credit crunches.
signals.drivers: Default expectations, risk appetite, rates, private-credit stress, fund outflows.

rubric.alert: HY OAS > 6.0%, or widened > 200bp in a month.
rubric.watch: HY OAS 4.0–6.0%, or widened > 100bp in a month.
rubric.normal: US HY option-adjusted spread < 4.0%.

signals.name: US dollar
signals.why: The dollar is the world's funding currency; violent moves squeeze emerging markets and anyone with dollar debts.
signals.drivers: Fed vs other central banks, safe-haven demand, trade policy, reserve diversification.

rubric.alert: DXY moved > 8% in 3 months, or dollar funding stress (Fed swap lines drawn materially).
rubric.watch: DXY moved 5–8% in 3 months, or outside 90–108.
rubric.normal: DXY moved < 5% over 3 months and is between 90 and 108.

signals.name: Banking system stress
signals.why: Bank failures turn market losses into credit crunches; 2008 and 2023 both began as 'contained' bank problems.
signals.drivers: Rate shocks to bond portfolios, commercial property losses, deposit flight, private-credit links.

rubric.alert: STLFSI > 1.5, or ECB CISS > 0.45, or a systemically important bank fails or needs rescue, or emergency central-bank facilities launched.
rubric.watch: STLFSI 0–1.5, or ECB CISS 0.25–0.45, or a mid-sized bank failure/rescue, or a large bank under visible funding pressure.
rubric.normal: St Louis Fed Financial Stress Index < 0, ECB CISS < 0.25, and no notable bank failures or rescues.

signals.name: Gold (fear gauge)
signals.why: Gold is the oldest crisis hedge; disorderly surges signal fear about currencies, inflation or geopolitics.
signals.drivers: Real interest rates, central-bank buying, geopolitical fear, dollar moves.

rubric.alert: 3-month gain > 20%, or a single-week move > 7% either way.
rubric.watch: 3-month gain 10–20%, or a fall > 8%.
rubric.normal: 3-month change between −8% and +10%.

signals.name: Crypto stress
signals.why: Crypto is now plumbed into mainstream finance via ETFs and stablecoins; a crash or de-peg can spill into funding markets.
signals.drivers: Liquidity, leverage, regulation, stablecoin reserves, exchange solvency.

rubric.alert: Drawdown > 45%, or a major stablecoin de-pegs (> 3% for > 24h), or a top-10 exchange fails.
rubric.watch: Drawdown 25–45%, or a top-10 exchange/stablecoin under stress.
rubric.normal: Bitcoin drawdown from 52-week high < 25% and no major stablecoin/exchange incidents.

signals.name: Dollar funding stress
signals.why: Overnight dollar funding is the plumbing of global finance; repo-rate spikes came before the market seizures of September 2019 and March 2020.
signals.drivers: Bank reserves, Treasury issuance and cash balances, quarter-end window dressing, Fed balance-sheet policy.

rubric.alert: SOFR more than 25bp above IORB, or Fed repo operations above $50bn in a day, or emergency Fed liquidity facilities.
rubric.watch: SOFR 10–25bp above IORB on any day in the past week (the top ~10% of weeks since 2024), or Fed repo operations of $15–50bn in a day.
rubric.normal: SOFR less than 10bp above the Fed's interest on reserves (IORB) on every day of the past week, and Fed repo operations under $15bn.

signals.name: Private credit stress
signals.why: Private credit has grown fast outside bank regulation; its losses surface late and can spill into banks, insurers and pension funds.
signals.drivers: Defaults among leveraged mid-sized borrowers, payment-in-kind interest, fund redemption requests, bank lending to funds.

rubric.alert: Several large funds gate at once, forced asset sales, or losses spreading to banks or insurers.
rubric.watch: A large fund limits redemptions, listed BDCs trade at wide discounts to NAV, or a cluster of borrower defaults with heavy losses.
rubric.normal: No notable fund gates, defaults or markdowns beyond the routine.

signals.name: Yen & carry trade
signals.why: Cheap yen borrowing funds positions worldwide; a sharp yen rally forces those trades to unwind, as in the global sell-off of August 2024.
signals.drivers: Bank of Japan policy, the US–Japan rate gap, JGB yields, currency intervention, risk appetite.

rubric.alert: A move of more than 5% in a week or 10% in a month, with stress spreading to other markets.
rubric.watch: A 3–5% move in a week, a 6–10% move in a month, or Japanese currency intervention.
rubric.normal: The yen moves less than 3% against the dollar in a week and less than 6% in a month.

signals.name: US recession risk
signals.why: A US recession drags world trade, earnings and jobs; it is the single biggest swing factor for the global cycle.
signals.drivers: Labour market, consumer spending, credit conditions, rates and fiscal policy.

rubric.alert: Sahm ≥ 0.50, or two consecutive negative GDP quarters, or NBER declares recession.
rubric.watch: Sahm 0.30–0.49, or one negative GDP quarter, or payrolls negative in a release.
rubric.normal: Sahm rule indicator < 0.30 and no negative GDP quarter in the latest two releases.

signals.name: US inflation
signals.why: Inflation sets Fed policy and thus global borrowing costs; a resurgence would keep rates high for everyone.
signals.drivers: Energy, tariffs, wages, housing costs, supply chains.

rubric.watch: CPI 3.0–4.5%, or rising for 3 consecutive months.
rubric.normal: Headline CPI y/y < 3.0%.

signals.name: Euro-area economy
signals.why: The euro area is the UK's largest trading partner; stagnation there hits UK exports and European markets.
signals.drivers: Energy prices, German industry, ECB policy, fiscal rules, China demand.

rubric.alert: Technical recession, or PMI < 45, or bond-spread fragmentation forcing ECB action.
rubric.watch: Stagnation (GDP ~0), or composite PMI 45–50.
rubric.normal: Positive GDP growth and composite PMI > 50.

signals.name: China economy
signals.why: China is the world's factory and the biggest marginal buyer of commodities; a hard landing would ripple through every supply chain.
signals.drivers: Property sector, local-government debt, exports and tariffs, deflation, stimulus.

rubric.alert: Hard landing (growth < 3%), financial contagion, or capital controls tightened sharply.
rubric.watch: Deflation, renewed property-developer defaults, or growth clearly below target.
rubric.normal: Growth near official target, stable property sales, no financial contagion.

signals.name: Central bank stress
signals.why: Central banks are the shock absorbers; when they are boxed in or their independence is challenged, markets lose their backstop.
signals.drivers: Inflation vs growth trade-off, political pressure, currency moves, financial stability.

rubric.alert: Emergency inter-meeting moves, attempt to remove a central-bank head, or coordinated intervention.
rubric.watch: Stagflationary dilemma, open political pressure on a major central bank, or FX intervention by a G7 bank.
rubric.normal: Fed, ECB and BoJ acting orderly and on schedule; independence unquestioned.

signals.name: Sovereign debt stress
signals.why: When big governments struggle to borrow, it raises everyone's costs and can force sudden austerity or money-printing.
signals.drivers: Deficits, auction demand, ratings actions, political shocks, long-end yields.

rubric.alert: Failed G7 auction, emergency central-bank purchases, France–Bund > 150bp, or Italy–Bund > 250bp.
rubric.watch: G7 30-year yields at multi-decade highs, a G7 downgrade, or France–Bund 80–150bp / Italy–Bund 150–250bp.
rubric.normal: Auctions orderly; France–Bund spread < 80bp; Italy–Bund < 150bp; no G7 downgrades this month.

signals.name: Global activity (PMI)
signals.why: Purchasing-manager surveys are the fastest read on whether the world economy is expanding or contracting.
signals.drivers: Orders, inventories, trade policy, energy costs, credit conditions.

rubric.alert: Global composite < 49.
rubric.watch: Global composite 49–51, or manufacturing < 49.
rubric.normal: J.P.Morgan Global Composite PMI > 51.

signals.name: US jobless claims
signals.why: Weekly claims are the earliest hard data on US layoffs; a sustained rise usually comes before the unemployment rate turns.
signals.drivers: Layoffs, hiring freezes, federal job cuts, storms, strikes and seasonal quirks.

rubric.alert: More than 30% above its 52-week low.
rubric.watch: 15–30% above its 52-week low.
rubric.normal: The 4-week average of initial claims is less than 15% above its 52-week low.

signals.name: Emerging-market stress
signals.why: Energy-importing and heavily indebted emerging economies crack first in oil shocks and strong-dollar periods, with knock-on defaults and unrest.
signals.drivers: Oil and food import bills, dollar strength, FX reserves, debt maturities, IMF programmes.

rubric.alert: A sovereign default or capital controls in a major emerging economy, or several in crisis at once.
rubric.watch: A major emerging economy's currency falls more than 10% in a month, its reserves fall fast, or it seeks emergency IMF support.
rubric.normal: No major emerging economy in acute currency or debt distress.

signals.name: Oil (Brent)
signals.why: Oil feeds inflation, transport and household budgets; price spikes have preceded most post-war recessions.
signals.drivers: OPEC+ output, Middle East supply risk, sanctions, demand, inventories, shipping disruption.

rubric.alert: Brent > $110, or 1-month change > +30%, or a major physical supply outage (> 2 mb/d).
rubric.watch: Brent $85–110, or 1-month change +15–30%.
rubric.normal: Brent < $85 and 1-month change < +15%.

signals.name: European gas (TTF)
signals.why: European gas sets UK and EU power prices and heating bills; Europe has had no cushion since losing Russian pipeline gas.
signals.drivers: LNG supply, storage levels, weather, Norwegian outages, Middle East LNG routes.

rubric.alert: TTF > €70/MWh, or a major supply cut-off (e.g. Qatar LNG or Norway outage > 1 week).
rubric.watch: TTF €40–70/MWh, or storage > 10 points below seasonal norm.
rubric.normal: TTF < €40/MWh and EU storage at or above seasonal norm.

signals.name: Shipping chokepoints
signals.why: Around 30% of seaborne oil and much container trade passes Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb/Suez, Panama and Malacca; disruption raises prices worldwide.
signals.drivers: Houthi/Iran attacks, war-risk insurance, drought (Panama), naval incidents, piracy.

rubric.alert: Hormuz traffic materially impeded, or any chokepoint closed, or two or more disrupted at once.
rubric.watch: One chokepoint disrupted (attacks, large-scale diversions, draught restrictions).
rubric.normal: All major chokepoints operating normally.

signals.name: Container freight
signals.why: Container rates feed through to goods prices months later; spikes are an early inflation and supply-chain warning.
signals.drivers: Chokepoint diversions, capacity, demand, port congestion, tariffs front-running.

rubric.alert: WCI > $4,000/FEU, or > +60% in a month.
rubric.watch: WCI $2,500–4,000/FEU, or +30–60% in a month.
rubric.normal: Drewry World Container Index < $2,500/FEU and 1-month change < +30%.

signals.name: Global food prices
signals.why: Food prices drive inflation, hunger and political unrest; poorer countries spend up to half of income on food.
signals.drivers: Harvests, weather, fertiliser and energy costs, export bans, conflict in breadbaskets.

rubric.alert: FFPI > 135, or multiple major exporters ban exports of a staple.
rubric.watch: FFPI 120–135, or y/y > +5%, or a major exporter restricts exports.
rubric.normal: FAO Food Price Index < 120 and y/y change < +5%.

signals.name: Critical minerals
signals.why: Rare earths, gallium, germanium and graphite are chokepoints for chips, EVs and defence — and China dominates processing.
signals.drivers: Export controls, trade disputes, mine outages, stockpiling.

rubric.alert: Export bans in force that are causing reported production stoppages outside China.
rubric.watch: New export controls announced or licensing slowed.
rubric.normal: No new export restrictions in the past month.

signals.name: Fertiliser supply
signals.why: Fertiliser prices lead food prices by months; much of the world's urea and ammonia is exported from Russia, the Gulf and China.
signals.drivers: Gas prices, Gulf shipping, export bans and quotas, sanctions, planting seasons.

rubric.alert: Urea up more than 60% in three months, several major exporters restricting at once, or a key export route closed.
rubric.watch: Urea up more than 30% in three months, or a major exporter restricts exports.
rubric.normal: Urea and ammonia prices within their normal range; no major export restrictions.

signals.name: Nuclear plant safety
signals.why: Fighting near nuclear power plants risks a radiological release; the IAEA reports on Zaporizhzhia and other plants in or near war zones.
signals.drivers: Off-site power losses, strikes near plants, staffing, cooling water, military occupation.

rubric.alert: Damage to safety-critical systems, an INES level 2 or higher event, or a radiological release.
rubric.watch: A plant loses all off-site power, strikes land near a plant, or the IAEA reports a deteriorating safety situation.
rubric.normal: No new IAEA safety concerns at plants in or near conflict zones.

signals.name: US–China / Taiwan
signals.why: The world's two largest economies; a Taiwan crisis would halt most advanced chip supply and risk great-power war.
signals.drivers: PLA exercises, tariffs and tech controls, diplomacy, Taiwan politics, South China Sea incidents.

rubric.alert: Blockade or 'quarantine' of Taiwan, military clash, or severed diplomatic channels.
rubric.watch: Large-scale PLA exercises around Taiwan, major new sanctions/controls, or a naval/air incident.
rubric.normal: Managed relations; dialogue channels open; routine PLA activity.

signals.name: Russia–NATO
signals.why: Direct Russia–NATO confrontation is the most likely path to a European war involving the UK.
signals.drivers: Airspace and drone incursions, sabotage, Baltic incidents, nuclear signalling, Ukraine war spillover.

rubric.alert: Article 4 consultations, a direct military clash, or an attack on NATO territory.
rubric.watch: Airspace/drone violations, sabotage attributed to Russia, or explicit threats against members.
rubric.normal: No notable incidents on NATO territory in the past two weeks.

signals.name: Iran nuclear programme
signals.why: A nuclear-armed Iran — or strikes to prevent one — could ignite the Gulf and send oil far higher.
signals.drivers: Enrichment levels, IAEA access, Israeli/US military posture, snapback sanctions, talks.

rubric.alert: Strikes on nuclear sites, NPT withdrawal, or evidence of weaponisation.
rubric.watch: Enrichment at ≥ 60% or inspector access curtailed, or credible strike threats.
rubric.normal: IAEA access and active diplomacy; no escalation.

signals.name: Korean peninsula
signals.why: North Korea is a nuclear state with ICBMs; tension here involves the US, China, Japan and Russia simultaneously.
signals.drivers: Missile tests, Russia–DPRK military cooperation, US–ROK exercises, border incidents.

rubric.alert: Nuclear test, ICBM overflight of Japan, or military clash.
rubric.watch: Ballistic or cruise missile launches, or troop deployments abroad.
rubric.normal: No missile launches in two weeks; no border incidents.

signals.name: Trade war & tariffs
signals.why: Tariffs raise prices, reroute supply chains and slow growth; escalation cycles hurt export-heavy economies like the UK's partners.
signals.drivers: US tariff policy, retaliation, court rulings, trade deals, WTO disputes.

rubric.alert: Broad new tariffs in force with retaliation under way, or US average effective tariff rising sharply.
rubric.watch: New major tariffs announced or threatened between large economies.
rubric.normal: Tariff regime stable; no new major measures in the past two weeks.

signals.name: Sanctions & coercion
signals.why: Sanctions are now a frontline weapon; secondary sanctions and asset seizures fragment global finance and trade.
signals.drivers: Russia/Iran sanctions packages, secondary sanctions, frozen-asset decisions, export controls.

rubric.alert: Major economy cut off from payment systems, or large-scale seizure of sovereign assets.
rubric.watch: Major new packages, secondary-sanction threats on large economies, or asset-seizure moves.
rubric.normal: No major new sanctions packages this week.

signals.name: Political instability
signals.why: Coups, contested elections and constitutional crises in large economies unsettle markets, alliances and policy.
signals.drivers: Elections, government collapses, coups, emergency rule, mass protest movements.

rubric.alert: Coup or constitutional crisis in a G20 country, or deadly unrest threatening a G20 government.
rubric.watch: Government collapse or contested election in a G20 country, or a coup anywhere.
rubric.normal: No G20 government collapse, contested election or coup in the past month.

signals.name: Europe hybrid attacks
signals.why: Sabotage, arson and drone incursions over airports and bases are how state confrontation reaches daily life in the UK and Europe.
signals.drivers: Russia–NATO tensions, drone and cyber capabilities, proxy recruitment, elections.

rubric.alert: Repeated airport or infrastructure shutdowns across several countries, or sabotage causing casualties or a major outage.
rubric.watch: Drone incursions close an airport or military base, or a sabotage incident is attributed to a state.
rubric.normal: No significant attributed sabotage or airspace incursions in Europe this week.

signals.name: Russia–Ukraine
signals.why: Europe's largest war since 1945 shapes European security, energy, food exports and defence budgets.
signals.drivers: Front-line offensives, strike campaigns on energy, Western aid, negotiations, nuclear plant safety.

rubric.alert: Significant escalation — major new offensive, mass-casualty strikes, a nuclear-plant safety incident, or new state involvement.
rubric.watch: Active war at sustained intensity, or a ceasefire under strain.
rubric.normal: Ceasefire or peace deal holding.

signals.name: Israel, Gaza & region
signals.why: Conflict involving Israel, Gaza, Lebanon, Syria and Yemen threatens civilians, shipping and wider escalation. Direct hostilities with Iran are tracked under Gulf / US–Iran war.
signals.drivers: Ceasefire status, Iran-linked groups, hostage talks, humanitarian access, US posture.

rubric.alert: Multi-front escalation, major cross-border strikes between Israel and its neighbours, or mass-casualty events.
rubric.watch: Ongoing hostilities on one front, or a ceasefire repeatedly violated.
rubric.normal: Ceasefires holding across fronts (Gaza, Lebanon, Syria, Yemen).

signals.name: Sudan
signals.why: The world's largest displacement and hunger crisis; regional spillover into Chad, South Sudan and the Red Sea.
signals.drivers: SAF–RSF fighting, sieges, foreign arms supplies, aid access, famine.

rubric.alert: Major sieges or massacres reported, or famine spreading to new areas.
rubric.watch: Active war at sustained intensity.
rubric.normal: Ceasefire holding and aid flowing.

signals.name: DR Congo (east)
signals.why: A long war over mineral-rich territory, drawing in Rwanda and threatening a wider Great Lakes conflict.
signals.drivers: M23/AFC advances, Rwanda involvement, peace deals, mineral trade.

rubric.alert: Capture of a major city, or direct interstate fighting.
rubric.watch: Active fighting or a fragile ceasefire.
rubric.normal: Peace agreements holding; no major offensives.

signals.name: Sahel insurgency
signals.why: Jihadist groups control growing territory across Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger, driving displacement and coastal-state spillover.
signals.drivers: JNIM/IS-Sahel offensives, juntas, Russian forces, blockades, coastal-state attacks.

rubric.alert: Blockade or fall of a capital or major city, or mass-casualty attacks spreading to coastal states.
rubric.watch: Sustained insurgency at current levels.
rubric.normal: Declining violence trend.

signals.name: Myanmar
signals.why: A multi-sided civil war affecting 50 million people, with spillover to China, Thailand, India and Bangladesh.
signals.drivers: Resistance offensives, junta airstrikes, Chinese mediation, elections, humanitarian access.

rubric.alert: Major city falls, mass-casualty airstrikes, or cross-border escalation.
rubric.watch: Civil war at sustained intensity.
rubric.normal: Nationwide ceasefire holding.

signals.name: India–Pakistan
signals.why: Two nuclear-armed neighbours with a history of rapid escalation after terrorist attacks.
signals.drivers: Kashmir attacks, Line of Control firing, water disputes (Indus), domestic politics.

rubric.alert: Cross-border military strikes or mobilisation.
rubric.watch: Ceasefire violations, a major terrorist attack with blame assigned, or treaty suspensions.
rubric.normal: Ceasefire holding along the Line of Control; no major attacks.

signals.name: Nuclear risk
signals.why: Nuclear use anywhere would be a civilisational shock; arms-control treaties are weaker than at any time since the 1960s.
signals.drivers: Threats in active wars, testing, doctrine changes, arms-control collapse, proliferation.

rubric.alert: A nuclear test, changes in deployment/alert levels, or threatened use in an active conflict.
rubric.watch: Explicit threats, unusual exercises, doctrine changes, or arms-control lapses without replacement.
rubric.normal: No explicit nuclear threats or tests; arms-control dialogue active.

signals.name: Gulf / US–Iran war
signals.why: Direct hostilities between Iran and the US or Israel threaten Gulf energy infrastructure, the Strait of Hormuz and the wider region.
signals.drivers: Strikes and retaliation, attacks on shipping and Gulf states, mediation and ceasefire talks, US force posture.

rubric.alert: Active strikes between states, attacks on Gulf energy infrastructure or shipping, or the Strait of Hormuz substantially closed.
rubric.watch: A ceasefire or stalemate with sporadic strikes, or credible threats of renewed strikes.
rubric.normal: No direct state-on-state hostilities; diplomacy active.

signals.name: Other armed conflicts
signals.why: Wars and flashpoints outside Canary's named list — such as Yemen, Haiti, Ethiopia–Eritrea, Afghanistan–Pakistan, Libya and Somalia — can escalate with little warning.
signals.drivers: Coups, border clashes, insurgencies, state collapse, outside intervention.

rubric.alert: A new interstate war, a capital under attack, or mass-atrocity warnings in a conflict not tracked elsewhere.
rubric.watch: Crisis Group's CrisisWatch or credible reporting shows a significant deterioration in a conflict not tracked elsewhere.
rubric.normal: No conflict outside the named list is escalating sharply.

signals.name: Atlantic hurricanes
signals.why: Atlantic hurricanes hit the US Gulf coast, Caribbean and Central America — and refinery and insurance markets with them.
signals.drivers: Sea-surface temperatures, ENSO, wind shear, season timing (Jun–Nov peak Aug–Oct).

rubric.alert: Category 3+ landfall expected within 72 hours or occurring.
rubric.watch: Tropical storm or hurricane threatening land within 5 days.
rubric.normal: No hurricane active, or none threatening land within 5 days.

signals.name: Pacific & Indian cyclones
signals.why: Typhoons and cyclones are the deadliest weather events, threatening densely populated coasts in Asia and the Indian Ocean.
signals.drivers: Ocean heat, ENSO phase, season (W Pacific peaks Jul–Oct; N Indian Apr–Jun & Oct–Dec).

rubric.alert: GDACS red cyclone alert, or a super-typhoon/severe cyclone landfall on a populated coast.
rubric.watch: GDACS orange cyclone alert, or a typhoon/cyclone threatening land within 72h.
rubric.normal: No GDACS orange/red tropical cyclone alerts.

signals.name: Extreme heat
signals.why: Heat is the deadliest weather hazard globally, straining power grids, crops and health systems.
signals.drivers: Heat domes, climate warming, season, humidity, urban heat islands.

rubric.alert: Deadly heatwave with top-tier official warnings across a large population.
rubric.watch: Heatwave warnings across a major region, or national temperature records.
rubric.normal: No major heatwaves affecting large populations.

signals.name: Wildfires
signals.why: Large fires destroy towns, cause hazardous smoke over continents and drive insurance losses.
signals.drivers: Drought, heat, wind, fuel load, ignition, season.

rubric.alert: Fires burning into populated areas with fatalities or mass evacuation, or GDACS red.
rubric.watch: Large fires forcing evacuations, or GDACS orange.
rubric.normal: No GDACS orange/red wildfire alerts and no major evacuations.

signals.name: Major floods
signals.why: Floods affect more people than any other hazard, displacing millions each year.
signals.drivers: Extreme rainfall, monsoons, cyclones, snowmelt, dam failures.

rubric.alert: GDACS red flood alert, or > 100 deaths in a single event.
rubric.watch: GDACS orange flood alert, or a flood displacing > 50,000.
rubric.normal: No GDACS orange/red flood alerts.

signals.name: Earthquakes & tsunami
signals.why: Large earthquakes can kill thousands in seconds and disrupt global supply chains (chips, cars).
signals.drivers: Tectonics — unpredictable; impact depends on depth, location and building standards.

rubric.alert: PAGER red, or a tsunami causing damage.
rubric.watch: M7+ in the past 7 days, or PAGER orange, or a tsunami warning issued.
rubric.normal: No USGS PAGER orange/red alert and no M7+ in the past 7 days.

signals.name: Volcanic & aviation ash
signals.why: Major eruptions ground flights (Iceland 2010) and can cool the climate for years.
signals.drivers: Volcanic unrest; impact depends on ash plume height and jet-stream direction.

rubric.alert: Major airspace closures from ash, or a VEI 4+ eruption.
rubric.watch: Aviation colour code orange/red at a volcano near major air routes, or a large eruption.
rubric.normal: No aviation colour code red; no large eruptions.

signals.name: Drought
signals.why: Drought slowly destroys harvests, hydropower and river shipping, and drives famine and migration.
signals.drivers: Rainfall deficits, heat, ENSO, groundwater depletion.

rubric.alert: Drought driving famine conditions, a major exporter's harvest failure, or monsoon failure across a major breadbasket.
rubric.watch: Severe drought in a major crop region, a major river at record low, or a monsoon running more than 20% below normal.
rubric.normal: No major breadbasket in severe drought.

signals.name: Space weather
signals.why: Severe solar storms can disrupt satellites, GPS, HF radio and power grids.
signals.drivers: Solar flares and coronal mass ejections; solar cycle 25 is near its peak.

rubric.watch: G3, S2 or R3.
rubric.normal: NOAA scales G0–G2, S0–S1, R0–R2.

signals.name: Cold waves & winter storms
signals.why: Severe cold and winter storms kill, cut power and spike gas demand, as in Texas in 2021; they matter most when energy supplies are tight.
signals.drivers: Polar vortex disruption, blocking highs, ENSO, Arctic outbreaks.

rubric.alert: Deadly cold or winter storms with widespread power or gas outages.
rubric.watch: Top-tier cold or winter-storm warnings across a major region, or a cold wave lifting gas demand sharply.
rubric.normal: No major cold wave or winter storm affecting large populations.

signals.name: Global temperature
signals.why: Global temperature is the master climate variable; each tenth of a degree raises extreme-weather risk.
signals.drivers: Greenhouse gases, El Niño/La Niña, aerosols, solar cycle.

rubric.alert: > +1.6°C, or a record high for the calendar date.
rubric.normal: Daily global anomaly < +1.3°C above pre-industrial (ERA5 vs 1991–2020 + 0.88°C).

signals.name: Polar sea ice
signals.why: Sea ice reflects sunlight and regulates ocean circulation; record lows accelerate warming.
signals.drivers: Air and ocean temperatures, winds, season.

rubric.alert: Either pole at a record low for the calendar date.
rubric.watch: Either pole below −1.0 million km².
rubric.normal: Arctic and Antarctic extent anomalies both above −1.0 million km² vs 1981–2010.

signals.name: Atmospheric CO₂
signals.why: CO₂ concentration is the main long-run driver of warming; the growth rate shows whether emissions cuts are biting.
signals.drivers: Fossil emissions, land sinks, El Niño (weakens sinks), wildfires.

rubric.normal: Year-on-year growth < 2.0 ppm.

signals.name: El Niño / La Niña
signals.why: ENSO reshapes global weather for a year at a time — droughts, floods, hurricanes and crop yields.
signals.drivers: Pacific trade winds and ocean heat content.

rubric.alert: |ONI| ≥ 1.5 (strong event).
rubric.watch: |ONI| 0.5–1.5 (weak/moderate event).
rubric.normal: Oceanic Niño Index between −0.5 and +0.5 (neutral).

signals.name: Coral bleaching
signals.why: Reefs support a quarter of marine species and coastal economies; mass bleaching is a direct sign of ocean heat stress.
signals.drivers: Marine heatwaves, El Niño, warming trend.

rubric.alert: Bleaching extent at record levels with active new alerts in the past month.
rubric.watch: Global bleaching event in progress, or regional mass bleaching.
rubric.normal: No global bleaching event in progress.

signals.name: WHO emergencies
signals.why: A WHO Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) or 'pandemic emergency' is the top official global health alarm.
signals.drivers: Outbreak spread, IHR Emergency Committee decisions.

rubric.alert: A new PHEIC declared in the past 30 days, or a pandemic emergency declared.
rubric.watch: A PHEIC in effect, or an IHR Emergency Committee convened.
rubric.normal: No PHEIC in effect other than long-running polio.

signals.name: Ebola & haemorrhagic fevers
signals.why: Ebola, Marburg and similar viruses kill a large share of those infected; outbreaks that reach cities or cross borders can overwhelm health systems.
signals.drivers: Surveillance and contact tracing, vaccine availability (none licensed for some strains), conflict, cross-border travel, health-worker infections.

rubric.alert: More than 1,000 cases, or spread to a new country in the past 30 days.
rubric.watch: An active outbreak contained within one country, or fewer than 1,000 cases.
rubric.normal: No active Ebola/Marburg outbreak, or outbreaks declining with no new countries affected in 60 days.

signals.name: H5N1 bird flu
signals.why: H5N1 is the flu strain scientists most fear could become a pandemic; it has spread to mammals and dairy cattle.
signals.drivers: Human cases, mammal-to-mammal spread, mutations, surveillance.

rubric.alert: Confirmed sustained human-to-human transmission.
rubric.watch: Human clusters under investigation, rising human cases, or new mammalian species spread.
rubric.normal: Sporadic animal-to-human cases only.

signals.name: Mpox
signals.why: Clade I mpox is more severe and has spread beyond Central Africa.
signals.drivers: Case growth, vaccine access, travel-linked spread.

rubric.alert: PHEIC in effect with accelerating growth.
rubric.watch: Clade I spreading outside Africa or a regional surge.
rubric.normal: Cases declining; no PHEIC.

signals.name: Measles & vaccine-preventable
signals.why: Falling vaccination rates are bringing back diseases once eliminated; measles is the canary for the rest.
signals.drivers: Vaccine coverage, misinformation, health-system disruption.

rubric.alert: Multi-country surge with rising deaths, or polio/diphtheria resurgence in high-income countries.
rubric.watch: Large outbreaks in high-income countries, or loss of elimination status.
rubric.normal: No large outbreaks in high-income countries.

signals.name: Cholera & mosquito-borne
signals.why: Climate-sensitive diseases — cholera, dengue, chikungunya, Oropouche, West Nile and yellow fever — are hitting record levels and reaching new regions.
signals.drivers: Conflict, floods, heat, El Niño, water and sanitation, mosquito range expansion.

rubric.alert: Large outbreaks with high mortality in conflict zones, or a WHO grade 3 emergency.
rubric.watch: Record-level seasons, or local transmission in countries where the disease was not established (including Europe).
rubric.normal: Seasonal levels.

signals.name: Novel / unexplained outbreaks
signals.why: The next pandemic will start as an unexplained cluster; early signals matter.
signals.drivers: Surveillance reports, unknown illnesses, new pathogens.

rubric.alert: A novel pathogen with evidence of human-to-human spread across borders.
rubric.watch: An unexplained cluster or novel pathogen under investigation.
rubric.normal: No unexplained clusters under international investigation.

signals.name: Respiratory variants & flu
signals.why: Known viruses change; a new COVID-19 variant or a severe flu strain can strain health systems without being 'novel'.
signals.drivers: Viral evolution, waning immunity, seasonal patterns, vaccine match.

rubric.alert: WHO designates a variant of concern, or flu or COVID-19 hospitalisations strain several countries' health systems.
rubric.watch: WHO designates a new variant of interest, or a hemisphere's flu season is unusually early or severe.
rubric.normal: No WHO variant of interest rising fast; flu seasons of normal severity.

signals.name: Medicine shortages
signals.why: Shipping disruption, factory failures and export curbs can leave essential medicines short, as with US IV fluids after Hurricane Helene in 2024.
signals.drivers: Manufacturing concentrated in India and China, shipping, raw materials, demand spikes, regulation.

rubric.alert: Shortages forcing widespread rationing or cancelled treatment across major health systems.
rubric.watch: A shortage of an essential medicine or supply across several countries, or a UK Serious Shortage Protocol for a widely used medicine.
rubric.normal: No widespread shortages of essential medicines in major health systems.

signals.name: Major cyber incidents
signals.why: Ransomware and state hacking now shut down hospitals, retailers, carmakers and airports for weeks.
signals.drivers: Ransomware gangs, state actors, zero-days, supply-chain compromises.

rubric.alert: National-scale attack on critical infrastructure (power, health, finance), or a destructive state-attributed attack.
rubric.watch: Ransomware or attack disrupting a large company or critical service, or a mass-exploited zero-day.
rubric.normal: No major incidents disrupting critical services this week.

signals.name: Internet & cloud outages
signals.why: A handful of cloud and CDN providers carry much of the internet; one bad update can halt airlines, banks and payments.
signals.drivers: Software updates, configuration errors, attacks, power failures.

rubric.alert: Multi-hour global outage hitting payments, airlines or emergency services, ongoing or within 24h.
rubric.watch: A major cloud/CDN/payments outage > 2h in the past 48h.
rubric.normal: No major multi-hour outages in the past 48h.

signals.name: Undersea cables & GPS
signals.why: Subsea cables carry ~99% of intercontinental data; GPS jamming affects aviation and shipping.
signals.drivers: Anchor drags, sabotage, conflict-zone jamming and spoofing.

rubric.alert: Multiple cable cuts isolating a region, or confirmed sabotage.
rubric.watch: Cable damage incident, or widespread GNSS interference affecting aviation.
rubric.normal: No new cable cuts or major jamming escalations.

signals.name: Chip supply
signals.why: Advanced chips underpin everything from phones to AI to weapons; supply is concentrated in Taiwan and Korea.
signals.drivers: Export controls, Taiwan risk, fab outages, AI demand, materials.

rubric.alert: Major disruption to TSMC/Samsung output, or controls halting a major supply chain.
rubric.watch: New export controls, shortages reported in key segments, or a fab outage.
rubric.normal: Supply normal; no new major controls.

signals.name: AI incidents & governance
signals.why: Powerful AI systems are being deployed faster than safeguards; serious incidents or governance breakdowns carry systemic risk.
signals.drivers: Model releases, misuse incidents, regulation, compute controls, deepfakes in elections.

rubric.alert: AI-enabled attack on critical infrastructure, or AI-attributed mass harm event.
rubric.watch: A significant AI misuse incident, major deepfake disruption, or regulatory confrontation.
rubric.normal: No serious AI-attributed harm events or governance shocks this week.

signals.name: Exploited vulnerabilities
signals.why: Mass exploitation of a flaw in widely used software usually starts days or weeks before the breach headlines.
signals.drivers: Zero-days in edge devices and enterprise software, exploit sharing, slow patching, ransomware crews.

rubric.alert: An emergency directive or equivalent for mass exploitation of a ubiquitous product, with confirmed widespread compromise.
rubric.watch: 11 or more added in 7 days (the busiest ~5% of weeks since 2024), or mass exploitation of a widely used product.
rubric.normal: Fewer than 11 vulnerabilities added to CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue in the past 7 days.

signals.name: Famine
signals.why: Famine is the most extreme humanitarian failure, almost always man-made by conflict.
signals.drivers: War, sieges, aid access, harvest failure, funding cuts.

rubric.alert: Famine (IPC Phase 5) confirmed in at least one area.
rubric.watch: IPC Phase 5 projected or 'risk of famine' alerts.
rubric.normal: No IPC Phase 5 (Famine) classifications or projections.

signals.name: Forced displacement
signals.why: Over 120 million people are forcibly displaced; new mass displacement drives regional instability and migration politics.
signals.drivers: Conflict, disasters, persecution, economic collapse.

rubric.alert: A new event displacing > 1 million in a month.
rubric.watch: A new event displacing > 500,000 people in a month.
rubric.normal: No new mass displacement events this month.

signals.name: Civil unrest
signals.why: Mass protest and state crackdowns signal political fragility and can topple governments.
signals.drivers: Cost of living, elections, corruption, repression, food and fuel prices.

rubric.alert: Deadly nationwide unrest or a state crackdown in a major country.
rubric.watch: Significant protests in several countries or deadly unrest in one.
rubric.normal: No deadly mass unrest in large countries.

signals.name: Humanitarian funding gap
signals.why: When appeals go unfunded, food aid and health services are cut first; funding gaps lead famine and displacement by months.
signals.drivers: Donor budgets and aid cuts, new crises competing for funds, access constraints.

rubric.alert: Pipeline breaks forcing large-scale suspension of food or health aid in famine-risk countries.
rubric.watch: Funding more than 10 percentage points behind recent years at the same point, or major ration cuts announced.
rubric.normal: UN global appeal funding in line with recent years; no major ration cuts.

signals.name: UK inflation & rates
signals.why: UK inflation and the Bank Rate set mortgage, savings and business borrowing costs for the whole country.
signals.drivers: Energy prices, wages, services inflation, sterling, global rates.

rubric.alert: CPI > 4.0%, or an emergency BoE move.
rubric.watch: CPI 2.5–4.0%, or the BoE reversing course.
rubric.normal: CPI ≤ 2.5% and Bank of England moving gradually or on hold.

signals.name: Gilt market
signals.why: Gilt yields set UK mortgage rates and the government's borrowing costs; the 2022 LDI crisis showed how fast it can break.
signals.drivers: Fiscal credibility, BoE policy, inflation, global bond moves, pension-fund flows.

rubric.alert: BoE intervention, or 10y moved > 75bp in a month.
rubric.watch: 30y gilt at multi-decade highs, or 10y moved 40–75bp in a month, or a weak auction.
rubric.normal: 10y gilt moved < 40bp in a month and auctions orderly.

signals.name: UK energy price cap
signals.why: The Ofgem cap sets bills for most UK households — a direct cost-of-living signal.
signals.drivers: Wholesale gas and power prices, network costs, policy levies.

rubric.alert: Cap > £2,200, or forecast rise ≥ 20%.
rubric.watch: Cap £1,700–2,200, or forecast rise ≥ 5%.
rubric.normal: Typical dual-fuel cap < £1,700/yr and next forecast change < +5%.

signals.name: UK weather warnings
signals.why: Met Office warnings are the official signal for disruption to travel, power and safety in the UK.
signals.drivers: Storms, heavy rain, snow and ice, heat, fog, thunderstorms.

rubric.alert: Any red warning in force.
rubric.watch: Widespread yellow or any amber warning in force.
rubric.normal: No warnings, or only localised yellow warnings.

signals.name: NHS & respiratory
signals.why: Winter respiratory waves and NHS capacity directly affect access to care for everyone in the UK.
signals.drivers: Flu, COVID, RSV, norovirus, staffing, strikes.

rubric.alert: High or very high flu activity nationally, or widespread critical incidents.
rubric.watch: Respiratory activity above baseline and rising, or several trusts in critical incidents.
rubric.normal: Respiratory activity at baseline and no widespread critical incidents.

signals.name: UK terrorism threat level
signals.why: The official MI5 assessment of the likelihood of a terrorist attack in the UK.
signals.drivers: Intelligence assessment by JTAC.

rubric.alert: Severe or Critical.
rubric.watch: Substantial.
rubric.normal: Low or Moderate.

signals.name: UK strikes & disruption
signals.why: Strikes and infrastructure failures in rail, health, ports and power disrupt daily life and the economy.
signals.drivers: Pay disputes, infrastructure failures, cyber incidents, weather.

rubric.alert: Multiple simultaneous national strikes, or nationwide infrastructure failure.
rubric.watch: National strike in one sector or major infrastructure disruption.
rubric.normal: No national-scale strikes or disruption this week.

signals.name: GB energy supply margins
signals.why: When gas or electricity margins tighten, Britain risks price spikes and, at worst, controlled disconnections in winter.
signals.drivers: Gas imports and storage, wind output, interconnectors, plant outages, cold weather.

rubric.alert: A Gas Deficit Warning, a high risk of demand control notice, or demand control used.
rubric.watch: NESO issues an Electricity Margin Notice or capacity market notice, or National Gas issues a Gas Margins Notice.
rubric.normal: NESO and National Gas report adequate margins; no notices issued.

signals.name: UK flood warnings
signals.why: Flooding is the UK's most common natural hazard; Environment Agency flood warnings are separate from Met Office weather warnings.
signals.drivers: Heavy rain, saturated ground, storm surges, high river levels.

rubric.alert: Any severe flood warning (danger to life) in force in the UK.
rubric.watch: 10 or more flood warnings in force in England, or major flooding in Scotland, Wales or Northern Ireland.
rubric.normal: No severe flood warnings and fewer than 10 Environment Agency flood warnings in force.
